A step length $\alpha$ along $d$ from $x$ satisfies the *Wolfe curvature condition* with constant $\sigma$ if For a descent direction and $\sigma < 1$ this says that the directional derivative has increased by a definite fraction, which rules out steps that are too short. nodes.title: Wolfe curvature condition

nodes.summary: A step length $\alpha$ along $d$ from $x$ satisfies the *strong Wolfe conditions* with constants $\delta$ and $\sigma$ if it satisfies the Armijo condition and usually with $0 < \delta < \sigma < 1$. The classical convergence analyses of the Fletcher–Reeves, Polak–Ribière–Polyak and Hestenes–Stiefel conjugate gradient methods assume these conditions.
nodes.title: Strong Wolfe conditions

nodes.summary:
A step length satisfying the strong Wolfe conditions with constants $\delta, \sigma$ satisfies the standard Wolfe conditions with the same constants, since $
abla f(x + \alpha d)^	op d \ge -|
abla f(x + \alpha d)^	op d| \ge \sigma\, 
abla f(x)^	op d$. So every result proved under standard Wolfe steps, such as the Zoutendijk condition, holds under strong Wolfe steps.
nodes.title: Strong Wolfe steps are standard Wolfe steps

nodes.summary: A step length satisfies the *standard Wolfe conditions* with constants $\delta$ and $\sigma$ if it satisfies the Armijo condition with constant $\delta$ and the curvature condition with constant $\sigma$; one usually takes $0 < \delta < \sigma < 1$, which guarantees that such steps exist for a descent direction when $f$ is continuously differentiable and bounded below along the ray (Wolfe).
nodes.title: Standard Wolfe conditions
